rendered: The premise is reversed. The paper does not conclude that aqueous processing is incompatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[1]. It concludes the opposite. In its words: this work clearly demonstrates that aqueous processing is[2] compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[3]. The lithium leaching is real, but the paper treats it as minimal: even Ni-rich NMC 811 shows only minimal[4] Li+ leaching, with leaching (~3 wt%) after one week[5]. It also reports that the powders showed there are no bulk structural[6] changes after water exposure. Cell performance was close to the solvent-processed baseline: the aqueous-processed cells were slightly lower, (~70% vs. ~76%)[7], which the paper calls very good cycling performance. The paper does name open problems: Li+/H+ exchange and a rising pH, which it says must be handled through formulation work. It states that This approach could be applied to NMC 811[8] as well. So the paper's conclusion is that aqueous processing is compatible with Ni-rich NMC 811[9], and the leaching and pH issues are treated as problems to solve by formulation, not as a reason to rule out water-based processing.
